commit.message:
Stop a soreness save from silently deleting the entry

Saving with an empty muscle list meant "you cleared this entry", so it
fired a DELETE, swallowed the 404 when no such document existed, and
closed the editor as though the entry had been written. A legs entry
logged against the Aug 14 workout vanished exactly that way: the pod log
for the whole session holds one DELETE and no POST.

Three things were wrong, and they compound:

- "Change workout" reused the fresh-entry setup, so returning from the
  workout list emptied the muscles and reset the date to today even when
  the same workout was re-picked. That is the one confirmed way to reach
  an empty list without touching it.
- An empty save was a covert delete with no confirmation and no error.
- An entry naming no muscles could not be represented at all, which is
  what made "empty" read as "deleted" in the first place.

Now re-attributing keeps the date and muscles, an entry with no muscles
is a real entry that draws its stripe (the `peak` label just drops off),
and deleting is its own button rather than a side effect of emptying a
list.

Also drop the stripe opacity that encoded severity. Levels 3 and 5 came
out at 0.50 and 0.64 opacity against a dark ground, which is not a
readable difference; colour now means one thing, which workout. And the
source picker heading is a directive rather than a question, since it is
a required step in a flow and not a conversational field.
